name: Escalate and resolve risk limit breaches (one breach or threshold exception)
summary: The fund runs inside Board and management limits on total risk, leverage, liquidity, credit and concentration, with lower thresholds that act as early warnings. When the daily risk run or counterparty monitoring shows a limit or threshold exceeded, Risk validates and classifies the event, notifies the accountable department head, the CIO and the CFRO, judges the department's explanation or remediation plan, gets plans approved, tracks the measure until it is back inside, and reports every event to the monthly Investment Risk Committee and Board-level ones to the Board. Most of the elapsed time is waiting for markets or trades to bring the measure back and for the next committee meeting; the hard parts are telling data errors from real breaches and agreeing how fast a passive breach should be cured.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national pension fund investment manager with about 2,000 employees and a second-line Risk group under the CFRO that monitors Board and management limits daily.
baseline.notes: Modelled on the risk governance the model fund describes for fiscal 2020 to 2022 (Integrated Risk Policy, IRC chaired by the CFRO, Board Risk Committee). Breach procedures themselves are not published.

trigger: The daily risk run or counterparty credit monitoring issues a limit breach notice after a Risk principal or director has confirmed the measure is over a limit or threshold.
end_state: The measure is back within its limit or threshold, the breach is closed in the register and reviewed by the Investment Risk Committee, and Board-level breaches are reported to the Board Risk Committee; or the notice is withdrawn as a data error.

volume.seasonality: Clustered in volatile markets (for example March 2020), when passive breaches of leverage, liquidity and counterparty limits rise together.

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file's process map (2 to 12 a month); the organisation does not publish breach counts.
Org file role. About 190 minutes a breach for logging, tracking and the committee summary, at 6 breaches a month.

Org file role. Notification, assessment and negotiation, about 110 minutes a breach.
Org file role. Plan approval, overdue escalations and Board reporting.

steps.name: Record the breach notice in the breach register
steps.description: A Risk senior associate logs the notice from the daily risk run or the counterparty monitoring team in the breach register: the measure, the limit or threshold, the level reached, the date first exceeded and the accountable department.

evidence.note: Risk limits are a core element of a risk appetite framework (FSB); Risk monitors compliance with all limits and the Risk Policy holds breach procedures; register fields are estimates.

steps.name: Validate and classify the breach
steps.description: A Risk principal reruns or checks the measure and its inputs to rule out data or model errors, then classifies the event as a threshold exception, a management-level limit breach or a Board limit breach, and as active (caused by a trade) or passive (caused by market moves).

error.defect_description: A data error is treated as a real breach, or a real breach is dismissed.

control.basis: Risk Policy breach treatment and escalation procedures (Investment Statement s. 9.11)

next.condition: data or model error, notice withdrawn

evidence.note: Breach procedures sit in the Risk Policy; UCITS rules distinguish limits exceeded for reasons beyond the fund's control. Share of false alarms estimated.

steps.name: Notify the accountable executive, CIO and CFRO
steps.description: The Risk director emails the head of the accountable department, the Chief Investment Officer and the CFRO with the measure, limit, current level, cause as far as known and the response expected, and calls the department head for Board limits.

control.basis: Risk Policy escalation: Risk notifies the accountable department head and the CIO of limit breaches

next.condition: total fund limit owned by Total Fund Management
Capital Markets and Factor Investing limit or counterparty exposure

evidence.note: Risk is the second line over limits (F2022); prompt notification mirrors the one-business-day board report under SEC Rule 22e-4. Department split estimated from the process map and potential loss contributions.

steps.name: Total Fund Management explains the breach and proposes action
steps.description: The Total Fund Management group head responsible for the limit (leverage, liquidity, total risk or currency) reviews the breach notice with the portfolio team, explains what caused it (a trade, a market move, a valuation change or a data issue), and replies to Risk with either an explanation for a threshold exception or a remediation proposal with trades, hedges or limits on new activity and a target date.

evidence.note: First line owns the response under the three lines model (F2022); effort and response time estimated.

steps.name: Capital Markets and Factor Investing explains the breach and proposes action
steps.description: The head of Capital Markets and Factor Investing, for desk, strategy or counterparty exposure limits reviews the breach notice with the portfolio team, explains what caused it (a trade, a market move, a valuation change or a data issue), and replies to Risk with either an explanation for a threshold exception or a remediation proposal with trades, hedges or limits on new activity and a target date.

evidence.note: Counterparty and desk limits sit with CMF trading and financing; effort and response time estimated.

steps.name: Active Equities explains the breach and proposes action
steps.description: The head of Active Equities, for department risk budget, active risk or concentration limits reviews the breach notice with the portfolio team, explains what caused it (a trade, a market move, a valuation change or a data issue), and replies to Risk with either an explanation for a threshold exception or a remediation proposal with trades, hedges or limits on new activity and a target date.

evidence.note: Effort and response time estimated.

steps.name: Credit Investments explains the breach and proposes action
steps.description: The head of Credit Investments, for credit risk, concentration or department risk budget limits reviews the breach notice with the portfolio team, explains what caused it (a trade, a market move, a valuation change or a data issue), and replies to Risk with either an explanation for a threshold exception or a remediation proposal with trades, hedges or limits on new activity and a target date.

evidence.note: Effort and response time estimated.

steps.name: Risk assesses the explanation and remediation proposal
steps.description: The Risk director checks the stated cause against the data, judges whether a threshold exception can be accepted with monitoring, and for limit breaches whether the proposed trades and deadline cure the breach in reasonable time at acceptable cost, including whether a passive breach should be cured gradually.

control.basis: Three lines of defence: second line independently challenges the first line's response

evidence.note: Independent challenge by Risk (F2022); passive breach handling (UCITS Art. 57); shares estimated.

steps.name: Negotiate a stronger remediation plan with the department
steps.description: The Risk director meets the department team to agree faster or larger risk reduction, interim restrictions on new trades or an alternative hedge, and documents the revised plan and deadline.

evidence.note: Negotiation between second and first line is common practice; time estimated.

steps.name: Head of Risk approves the remediation plan and deadline
steps.description: The Managing Director, Head of Risk reviews the plan, the deadline and any interim restrictions, approves them or asks for changes, and decides whether the CFRO must approve because the breach is of a Board limit or is large.

control.basis: Risk Policy: remediation plans for limit breaches approved by the Head of Risk

next.condition: department remediates within its own portfolio

evidence.note: Risk reports to the CFRO (F2022); approval level and routing shares estimated.

steps.name: CFRO approves the plan and informs the CEO and Board chair
steps.description: The Chief Financial and Risk Officer approves the plan for Board-level or large breaches, informs the CEO and, for a Board limit, the chair of the Board's Risk Committee ahead of the formal report.

control.basis: Risk Policy and Board Risk Committee oversight of exceptions to risk policies

evidence.note: Board Risk Committee reviews exceptions (F2022); early board notice mirrors the one-business-day rule in SEC Rule 22e-4.

steps.name: CIO approves remediation trades through the Balancing Portfolio
steps.description: The Chief Investment Officer approves the size and timing of rebalancing trades in the Balancing Portfolio or other total fund levers needed to bring the measure back within its limit.

control.basis: Management authorities: CIO accountable for total fund exposures and rebalancing

evidence.note: The CIO recommends risk targets and the fund rebalances to stay within limits (F2022, Investment Statement s. 9.8); approval step estimated.

steps.name: Issue the remediation plan to the Balancing Portfolio team
steps.description: The Total Fund Management group head sends the approved plan with target exposures and deadline to the Balancing Portfolio team so it enters the next daily rebalancing review.

evidence.note: Hand-off to the daily rebalancing workflow, which lists Risk's remediation plan as a trigger.

steps.name: Track the breach until it is cured
steps.description: The senior associate checks the measure in each daily risk run against the plan, updates the breach register, reminds the department of the deadline and flags slippage to the director.

next.condition: measure back within limit or threshold

evidence.note: Plans to return within limits in a reasonable time, reassessed every 30 days (SEC Rule 22e-4), and passive breaches remedied as a priority (UCITS); time to cure estimated.

steps.name: Escalate an overdue remediation
steps.description: The Head of Risk raises the missed deadline with the department head and CIO, agrees an extended deadline or extra actions, and decides whether the CFRO must be involved.

control.basis: Risk Policy escalation of unremediated breaches

evidence.note: Ongoing reassessment of breach plans while a breach lasts (SEC Rule 22e-4 analogy); shares estimated.

steps.name: Confirm the cure and close the breach
steps.description: The principal confirms from the risk run that the measure has stayed within the limit, records the cure date, root cause and actions taken in the register, and closes the item.

control.basis: Breach register kept as evidence for internal audit and Board reporting

evidence.note: Closure step and evidence role estimated.

steps.name: Prepare the breach summary for the monthly Investment Risk Committee
steps.description: At month end the senior associate writes up each breach and threshold exception with cause, remediation, days outstanding and status for the monthly risk and limit summary that goes to the Investment Risk Committee.

evidence.note: The IRC monitors risk exposures (F2022); monthly summary timing matches the daily risk run workflow's month-end report.

steps.name: Investment Risk Committee reviews breaches and remediation
steps.description: At its monthly meeting the Investment Risk Committee, chaired by the CFRO, reviews the breaches and threshold exceptions, challenges repeat causes and decides whether a limit design change or a Board report is needed.

control.basis: Management committee structure: IRC oversight of market, credit, liquidity and leverage risk limits

evidence.note: IRC chaired by the CFRO with an active role in monitoring exposures (F2022); per-breach time estimated.

steps.name: Report the breach to the Board Risk Committee
steps.description: The Head of Risk writes the breach, its cause and remediation into the quarterly risk report for the Board's Risk Committee, and presents it with the CFRO at the next meeting.

control.basis: Investment Statement s. 9.10: limits and thresholds reported to the Board at least quarterly; Board Risk Committee reviews exceptions

evidence.note: Quarterly Board reporting (s. 9.10), Board committees receive reports on Risk Policy implementation (terms of reference) and five Risk Committee meetings in F2022; wait until the next meeting estimated.

exceptions.name: False alarm from data or model error
exceptions.description: Validation finds a stale price, missing position or proxy error behind the apparent breach and the notice is withdrawn.

exceptions.name: Inadequate remediation plan
exceptions.description: Risk judges the department's plan too slow or too small and negotiates a stronger one before approval.

exceptions.name: Overdue remediation
exceptions.description: The measure is still over the limit at the deadline, often because markets keep moving against a passive breach, and the Head of Risk extends the deadline or adds actions.

exceptions.name: Board limit breach
exceptions.description: A Board-level limit is exceeded; the CFRO approves the plan, informs the CEO and the Risk Committee chair, and the breach is reported to the Board.

exceptions.name: Market stress cluster
exceptions.description: In a market shock several leverage, liquidity and counterparty limits are breached in the same week and the same executives receive several notices at once, lengthening every response.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from breach notice to closure and review at the monthly Investment Risk Committee
benchmarks.population: Limit breaches and threshold exceptions at a large pension investment manager

evidence.note: Estimate: a few days to a few weeks to cure plus up to a month to the next monthly committee; comparable rules give one business day to report and 30 days before a plan is reassessed.

benchmarks.population: US registered open-end funds under SEC Rule 22e-4

evidence.note: Well above the minimum liquidity requirement.

pain_points.description: Apparent breaches caused by stale prices, missing positions or private asset proxies have to be ruled out before anyone is notified, delaying real escalations.

evidence.note: Aggregating exposures quickly and accurately is a known weakness (BCBS 239 background).

pain_points.description: Department heads answer breach notices between deal and portfolio work, so responses take a day or more.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Passive breaches caused by market moves can take weeks to cure without forced selling, and deadlines are often extended.

evidence.note: Rules for comparable funds allow cure in a reasonable time with periodic reassessment.

pain_points.description: Breaches are tracked in a spreadsheet register and written up by hand for the monthly committee, so status can lag the daily risk run.

evidence.note: Estimate based on the spreadsheet tools of the period.

assumptions: The process map's 2 to 12 events a month is kept; it includes threshold exceptions and department or desk limits. The daily risk run workflow issues formal notices on only about 1.6% of days for total fund limits, so most cases here come from department, desk and counterparty limits and escalated threshold warnings.
Department heads stand for their teams: their touch time covers their own review, while analysts' preparation is not counted separately.
Routing shares by department (TFM 40%, CMF 30%, AE 12%, CI 18%), the 56% share of threshold exceptions accepted with monitoring and the approval levels are estimates; the Risk Policy is not public.
Comparable regulatory rules for US mutual funds (SEC Rule 22e-4) and EU UCITS are cited as practice benchmarks; they do not apply to this organisation.
The remediation plan to the Balancing Portfolio team and the risk report to Board reporting are produced only on some paths, so their outcome is 'any'.
Loaded hourly costs come from the organisation file (overhead factor 1.25).
